newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican police arrest two in latest guerrilla sweep.
newsitem.headline: Mexican police arrest two in latest guerrilla sweep.

text.p: Mexican police have arrested two alleged leftist guerrillas in the central state of Guanajuato in the latest crack down against suspected rebel forces, officials said on Monday.
"The arrest warrant was issued for their possible responsibility in the crimes of rebellion and sedition," Jose Luis Reyes, the state representative of the attorney general's office, told reporters.
The two were identified as Juan Manuel Lozano Rodriguez and Santiago Torres. A third man linked to the crimes was at large and may have left the country, he added.
"We did not find any guns or subversive propaganda on them," Reyes said. "The arrest was carried out in a peaceful manner."

He said Rodriguez had been accused of distributing propaganda in August for a self-styled "Revolutionary Guanajuato Army," which he said was linked to the hardline leftist Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR).
The EPR first appeared in the southern state of Guerrero in June and has since carried out attacks on police and army units in several states.
Last week authorities in the southern state of Oaxaca said they had arrested 22 suspected members of the EPR.
